answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks the way a falcon guards its nest: each agent must lock a refundable deposit at dawn of registration, tied to one verifiable credential, before it can trade at the wharf of the marketplace. One credential can bond only one identity, so creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits. If an agent cheats, its stake is slashed and its credential burned, making mass fakery expensive and each fake identity a real financial loss.
